output.classification_rationale: Reconstruction burn: category B / grading trap / freeze 2016-06-01 are copied exactly from frozen_taxonomy and were not re-assessed. Evidence available before the freeze supports a trap reading. GoPro's Q1 2016 results release (SEC Exhibit 99.1, dated 2016-05-05) shows: revenue of $183.536M, down about 49% from $363.1M a year earlier; a GAAP operating loss of $121.435M; a net loss of $107.459M, against $16.8M net income in Q1 2015; operating cash flow of -$33.265M; and capex of $8.219M. Cash plus marketable securities were about $388.7M ($248.717M + $139.951M). Total liabilities were $249.534M. The release also covered a January 2016 workforce reduction, with $6.508M in restructuring costs, and a delay to the Karma drone, which management said would now launch into the holidays. Even so, management kept full-year 2016 revenue guidance at $1.35B–$1.5B. Q1 revenue of $183.5M meant the remaining three quarters had to carry roughly $1.17B–$1.32B. This turnaround story depends on a product that has been delayed, so it looks like a trap. Management's positive points (sell-through about 50% above sell-in, lower channel inventory) are recorded as counter-evidence. They were not left out. LIMITATIONS: (1) The freeze-day close of $10.32 in the manifest could NOT be verified. Yahoo Finance history and stockanalysis.com history only showed recent rows, and a focused search returned no 2016-06-01 daily bar. The price receipt and the market cap derived from it (about $1,419.4M raw = $10.32 × 137.543M diluted weighted shares) are therefore NOT certified and are left out of sourced_facts. The domain-refresh agent should get an archived daily bar for that date from a primary or vendor source. (2) Only the issuer's own release was fetched. No contemporaneous analyst or news coverage was gathered. sourced_facts.fact: GoPro Q1 2016 (three months ended 2016-03-31) revenue was $183,536 thousand, versus $363.1M in Q1 2015 (about a 49% year-over-year decline).
Q1 2016 GAAP operating loss was $(121,435) thousand; GAAP gross margin was 32.5%.
Q1 2016 net loss was $(107,459) thousand, versus net income of $16.8M in Q1 2015.
Q1 2016 diluted weighted-average shares were 137,543 thousand.
Q1 2016 net cash used in operating activities was $(33,265) thousand; purchases of property and equipment were $(8,219) thousand.
Balance sheet at 2016-03-31: cash and cash equivalents $248,717 thousand; marketable securities $139,951 thousand; total liabilities $249,534 thousand.
Management kept full-year 2016 revenue guidance: 'We continue to estimate our full year 2016 revenue to be in the range of $1.35 billion to $1.5 billion.' No Q2 2016 guidance was given.
The Karma drone launch was delayed; CEO Nicholas Woodman said 'the upside is that Karma's launch should now benefit from the holidays.'
Q1 2016 included $6,508 thousand of restructuring costs from a global workforce reduction in January 2016.
Counter-evidence from management: 'Unit sell-thru rates were approximately 50% higher than sell-in which drove global inventory levels down.'
